title: Don C NDE 4009
content: When I was fifteen years old, I had a bad deformity of my upper jaw. So my grandparents made arrangements to have an experimental surgery done. This surgery had only been done four times prior to this. While being operated on the surgeon severed an artery in my neck and I bleed to death. I remember floating in the corner of the room above the operating table looking down at myself wondering what was going on. Then all of a sudden I was pulled through this tunnel to a white light where I found myself standing on this golden brick road leading up to some kind of building that had twelve pillars along the side and front with steps leading up to a personage seated on a throne. This person got up and came down the stairs and down the road to me. All around me, I could see and feel a beautiful peace and tranquility with love and peace. I had no care in the world. Also as far as the eye could see to my left was a beautiful landscape of tulips of every color imaginable. To my right was a wall of a beautiful blue that matched the sky. I could not see beyond these barriers. When the person reached me, we spoke through thought. He told me that it was not my time to enter into my heavenly home but had a mission to fulfill and my life was going to be very hard. That I would go through many terrible experiences to the point of wanting to commit suicide but if I committed suicide I would not be allowed to come home. He told me that I would be watched over and protected, kept safe. If I would get through this mission, I would be allowed to return home. Then he waved his hand, a window in the wall to my right opened, and I could see my mother sitting in a chair in the hospital hallway crying. Then another window opened next to it. We stepped through it and into the kitchen of my home. We were standing on the kitchen floor behind my mother and she was at the kitchen sink peeling potatoes. The next thing I remember was waking up in a hospital bed. I spent six months in the hospital then released. I have had several experiences since then. Like when I was seventeen years old. I was out partying and four friends and I were going down a dirt road in a triumph convertible at 103 mph and he swerved hit the shoulder of the road into a tree. The car shot up the tree in the air flipping backwards and smashing into the ground it threw me five hundred yards in the air and out into a hay field. As I was falling, I was caught by someone in the convertible top of the car and lowered to the ground. When I got to the hospital I found out that I had hit the tree and ripped my liver but if I would have ripped it a quarter of an inch more it would have killed me. Then I joined the Marine Corp and went to Vet Nam where I fought in the infantry. I went through several battles somewhere we were overrun by the enemy with soldiers dying all around me bullets flying past me but never once was I worried or afraid. I was blown out of a house in Wai City when we were fighting in house to house and I was wounded. I found out that I had a sixth sense about others and death, I was able to tell if someone else was going to die. When I came home from Vietnam, I was stationed in California. I went to a party on the beach. When everyone else left I decided to go swimming it was about 6:00 pm. I knew nothing about the tide's going out at that time, as I swam I was pulled out into the ocean. When I look up, I could not see the shore. So I started to swim back and being trained in the Corp I was trained to swim in the ocean but I could not get back, I was being pulled out faster than I could swim in. Finally, I felt a peace come over me and I felt a presence with me then everything went blank and I came to, a quarter of a mile down the beach, lying face down in the sand. Since then I have had many thing bad happen to me to the points of suicide due to post-traumatic stress disorder, drugs and alcohol. I have tried to tell my story to others but religions and others dismiss it. I have been in several religious organizations and searched my whole life to find my mission and purpose in life but I still don't know what I am to do. I do a lot to help others who are going through the things I have and that is very satisfying, I wish I could do more to help. I have no idea why the spirit moved me to this page, there must be a reason because I have found that you always listen to the spirit when it speaks.

arrival.religious_figure_detail: A male-presenting “personage seated on a throne” who told him it was not his time to enter his “heavenly home,” gave warnings about suicide, and spoke telepathically.

environment.environment_other_detail: “golden brick road”; building with “twelve pillars”; wall “of a beautiful blue” to the right; tulips of every color to the left; steps and a throne.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: After being shown scenes through “windows” and stepping through one into his home kitchen, “The next thing I remember was waking up in a hospital bed.”
boundary_and_return.mission_detail: Told he “had a mission to fulfill,” his life would be “very hard,” and if he got through it he would be “allowed to return home.”

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Experimental jaw surgery; surgeon severed an artery in his neck and he reports he “bleed to death.”

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: “windows” opened in a wall showing his mother in the hospital hallway and then his home kitchen; he and the being “stepped through it.”
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE in operating room corner → pulled through tunnel → white light and heavenly scene/being → boundary/barriers and message/mission → return to body (woke in hospital bed).

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: A “golden brick road” leading to a pillared building and throne; a blue wall that opened “windows” to view (and step into) scenes on Earth (hospital hallway and his home kitchen).
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I remember floating in the corner of the room above the operating table looking down at myself…”; “I was pulled through this tunnel to a white light…”; “it was not my time to enter into my heavenly home but had a mission to fulfill…”; “if I committed suicide I would not be allowed to come home.”
